title: Mayer--Vietoris inverse-image comparison before extension of scalars
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $S$, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let $M$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $U,V$ be opens covering $X$. Use the cartesian base change and module pullbacks [def-pc-base-change] and Ext-based cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. For an open $W$, put $C(W,n)=H^n(W,M|_W)$ and $D(W,n)=H^n(W_S,(M|_W)_S)$; put $C_X(n)=H^n(X,M)$ and $D_X(n)=H^n(X_S,M_S)$. Let $b(W,n)$ and $b_X(n)$ be exactly H.baseChangeLinear of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. There exist $R$-linear maps $r_n:C_X(n)\to C(U,n)\times C(V,n)$, $d_n:C(U,n)\times C(V,n)\to C(U\cap V,n)$, $\delta_n:C(U\cap V,n)\to C_X(n+1)$ and $S$-linear maps $r'_n,d'_n,\delta'_n$ between the corresponding $D$ terms. Both rows begin injectively in degree zero and are exact at each of their three consecutive pairs in every degree. For all $x\in C_X(n)$, $r'_nb_X(n)(x)=(b(U,n)((r_nx)_1),b(V,n)((r_nx)_2))$; for all $(x,y)\in C(U,n)\times C(V,n)$, $d'_n(b(U,n)x,b(V,n)y)=b(U\cap V,n)d_n(x,y)$; and for all $z\in C(U\cap V,n)$, $\delta'_nb(U\cap V,n)z=b_X(n+1)\delta_nz$. No flatness, quasi-coherence, compactness, separatedness or local comparison bijectivity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01EB, cohomology-lemma-mayer-vietoris; Tag 02KH, coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, Mayer--Vietoris alternative. Inverse-image compatibility is the agent-expanded naturality step required by this alternative.

proof.text: Obtain the geometric Ext presentations and coefficient identifications from the new presentation lemma. Construct the six horizontal linear maps by transporting precomposition with mk₀(K.g), mk₀(K.f), and the Ext class of the short exact sequence (and its exact inverse image). Scalar compatibility of the presentations and associativity of Ext composition prove their linearity.

Apply Mathlib Ext.precomp_mk₀_injective_of_epi and Ext.contravariant_sequence_exact₂′, exact₁′ and exact₃′ to K and K.map G, then transport through the additive equivalences. This gives both initial injections and all three exact pairs in every degree.

Apply the lower additive equivalence to each proposed square. Substitute the vertical identities of the geometric presentation. For the restriction and difference squares, use Ext.mapExactFunctor_comp, Ext.mapExactFunctor_mk₀ and associativity. For the boundary square, additionally use Ext.mapExactFunctor_extClass. These identities give the three squares directly; no tensor extension or flatness enters.

lean.statement: theorem H.baseChangeLinear_mayerVietoris {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (M : X.Modules) (U V : X.Opens) (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤) : let A := fun (W : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) ↦ HOver (W.ι ≫ f) ((pullback W.ι).obj M) n let B := fun (W : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) ↦ HOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f)) (baseChangedModule (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f) ((pullback W.ι).obj M)) n let AX := fun n : ℕ ↦ HOver f M n let BX := fun n : ℕ ↦ HOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f) (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M) n let β := fun (W : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) ↦ H.baseChangeLinear (S := S) (W.ι ≫ f) ((pullback W.ι).obj M) n let βX := fun n : ℕ ↦ H.baseChangeLinear (S := S) f M n ∃ (r : ∀ n : ℕ, AX n →ₗ[R] A U n × A V n) (d : ∀ n : ℕ, A U n × A V n →ₗ[R] A (U ⊓ V) n) (δ : ∀ n : ℕ, A (U ⊓ V) n →ₗ[R] AX (n + 1)) (r' : ∀ n : ℕ, BX n →ₗ[S] B U n × B V n) (d' : ∀ n : ℕ, B U n × B V n →ₗ[S] B (U ⊓ V) n) (δ' : ∀ n : ℕ, B (U ⊓ V) n →ₗ[S] BX (n + 1)), Function.Injective (r 0) ∧ Function.Injective (r' 0) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Exact (r n) (d n) ∧ Function.Exact (d n) (δ n) ∧ Function.Exact (δ n) (r (n + 1))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Exact (r' n) (d' n) ∧ Function.Exact (d' n) (δ' n) ∧ Function.Exact (δ' n) (r' (n + 1))) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : AX n), r' n (βX n x) = (β U n (r n x).1, β V n (r n x).2)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : A U n × A V n), d' n (β U n x.1, β V n x.2) = β (U ⊓ V) n (d n x)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : A (U ⊓ V) n), δ' n (β (U ⊓ V) n x) = βX (n + 1) (δ n x))
